title: Phone Wrist Straps and Crossbody Cases: A Simple Way to Stop Dropping Your Phone
subtitle: How a wrist cuff or a phone necklace keeps your phone close, what each one costs, and what neither one can do.
excerpt: A wrist strap or crossbody case can catch a slipping phone and free up your hands. Here is how the Peak Design Mobile Cuff and Keebos crossbody options compare.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Most of us know the feeling. You reach for the railing, grab a grocery bag or fish for your keys, and the phone slides out of your hand and lands face down on the sidewalk. A cracked screen is annoying and can be expensive to fix.

A phone strap is a small, low-cost fix for that moment. It ties the phone to your wrist or hangs it across your body, so if it slips, it stays with you instead of hitting the floor. It also lets you carry the phone without holding it the whole time.
There are two main styles. A wrist strap, sometimes called a cuff, is a short loop that goes around your wrist and attaches to your phone. The phone hangs near your hand.
A crossbody case is a phone case with a long cord or chain, worn over one shoulder and across the chest like a small purse. Both hands stay free.

Peak Design's Mobile Cuff uses what the company calls the Micro Anchor connection system, which lets the phone be attached and removed easily. The Gadgeteer reports each anchor is rated to hold 50 pounds, far more than a phone weighs. That figure comes from the review, not from Peak's own page. Cases without a strap loop need an adapter, and the Gadgeteer says one is included. Gear Patrol says the adapter fits nearly any phone case. Peak's page did not say which cases the Cuff fits, so check before you buy. Keebos takes the other route: you buy a new clear case made for your exact phone model.
"The Mobile Cuff is the simplest and most affordable of the Straps" — Steve Mazzucchi, Gear Patrol, February 17, 2026

A strap catches a falling phone. It does not make the phone easier to grip, the buttons easier to press, or the screen easier to read, so it is not a full answer for stiff or shaky hands. It will not help if you tend to set the phone down and forget it, and it does not make calls louder. If those are the bigger problems, a big-button phone or a sound amplifier may serve you better. Keep in mind too that the Cuff only works with a case that has a loop or with the included adapter, and that we found no independent testing of these straps.

items: Comfort: if your wrist, neck or shoulder is painful when something hangs from it, a strap may not suit you. Some people may prefer a crossbody style if the wrist bothers them, or the reverse.
Fit with your case: the Cuff needs a case with a loop or the included adapter. A crossbody case like Keebos replaces your current case, so pick your exact phone model.
Attaching and removing: look for a connection that is easy for your fingers to work, since you will use it often.

Length: a crossbody cord or chain should hang at a height you can comfortably reach. Adjustable length can help. A similar Keebos case lists a 54-inch adjustable cord, and the Royal Chains strap is listed at 45 inches.
Snag risk: wrist and neck straps can catch on furniture or a cord, and a phone hanging from the wrist can swing.
Returns and stock: check the return policy, and confirm the item is in stock at checkout before you count on it as a gift.

Total cost: neither page shows a subscription or monthly fee. Keebos lists free US shipping, with taxes calculated at checkout. Peak's page showed a 10% bundle discount, but only when you buy two other accessories.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

For a wrist cuff, first check whether your case has a loop or needs the included adapter, and follow Peak Design's instructions for attaching it. Practice attaching and removing the phone a few times at home, sitting down, before you head out.

For a crossbody case, put the new case on your phone, attach the cord or chain, and adjust the length if it allows. As a general suggestion, pick a length where the phone is easy to reach, and make sure you can still use it comfortably before heading out.

A phone that dangles from one connection point can draw attention in crowds. Gear Patrol raised this concern about theft. On a busy bus or at a fair, you may prefer to keep the phone in your hand or tucked inside a coat.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: A strap will not change how you use your phone, but it can take one small worry off your list. If you drop your phone often, or just want your hands free while you walk the dog or carry the groceries, a cuff or crossbody case is an affordable thing to try.
